Many known risk factors may increase a woman's risk of developing ovarian cancer. The risk of developing ovarian cancer is related to the amount of time a woman spends ovulating.[[35]](#cite_note-CRUKRisks-35) Factors that increase the number of ovulatory cycles a woman undergoes may increase the risk of developing ovarian cancer.[[35]](#cite_note-CRUKRisks-35) During ovulation, cells are stimulated to divide. If this division is abnormally regulated, tumors may form, which can be malignant. Early menarche and late menopause increase the number of ovulatory cycles a woman undergoes in her lifetime, and so increase the risk of developing ovarian cancer.[[30]](#cite_note-Hoffman35-30)[[35]](#cite_note-CRUKRisks-35)[[36]](#cite_note-Gong13-36) Since ovulation is suppressed during pregnancy, not having children also increases the risk of ovarian cancer.[[36]](#cite_note-Gong13-36) Therefore, [women who have not borne children](/wiki/Nulliparity "Nulliparity") are at twice the risk of ovarian cancer than those who have.[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27) Both obesity and hormone replacement therapy also raise the risk.[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)

The risk of developing ovarian cancer is less for women who have fewer menstrual cycles, no menstrual cycles, [breastfeeding](/wiki/Breastfeeding "Breastfeeding"), take oral contraceptives, have multiple pregnancies, and have a pregnancy at an early age. The risk of developing ovarian cancer is reduced in women who have had [tubal ligation](/wiki/Tubal_ligation "Tubal ligation") (colloquially known as having one's "tubes tied"), both ovaries removed, or [hysterectomy](/wiki/Hysterectomy "Hysterectomy") (an operation in which the uterus is removed).[[28]](#cite_note-CDCsep2016-28) Age is also a risk factor.[[27]](#cite_note-Harrisons-27)[[21]](#cite_note-Gib2016-21) Non-genetic factors such as diabetes mellitus, high body mass index, and tobacco use are also risk factors for ovarian cancer.[[24]](#cite_note-Zhou_Z_2017._p_17-24)

According to the [Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") system, Rocky Mountain National Park has a [Subarctic climate](/wiki/Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate") with cool summers and year around precipitation (*Dfc*). According to the [United States Department of Agriculture](/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Agriculture "United States Department of Agriculture"), the Plant [Hardiness zone](/wiki/Hardiness_zone "Hardiness zone") at Bear Lake Ranger Station (9492 ft / 2893 m) is 5a with an average annual extreme minimum temperature of -15.2 °F (-26.2 °C), and 5a with an average annual extreme minimum temperature of -16.1 °F (-26.7 °C) at Beaver Meadows Visitor Center (7825 ft / 2385 m).[[36]](#cite_note-USDA-36)

The complex interactions of elevation, slope, exposure and regional-scale air masses determine the climate within the park,[[37]](#cite_note-LCCVP_primer_p._1-37)[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38) which is noted for its extreme weather patterns.[[38]](#cite_note-Weather-38) A "collision of air masses" from several directions produces some of the key weather events in the region. When cold arctic air from the north meets warm moist air from the [Gulf of Mexico](/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico") at the [Front Range](/wiki/Front_Range "Front Range"), "intense, very wet snowfalls with total snow depth measured in the feet" accumulate in the park.[[37]](#cite_note-LCCVP_primer_p._1-37)

Its [ten provinces and three territories](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") extend from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean, making it the [second-largest country by total area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"), with the [longest coastline](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_length_of_coastline "List of countries by length of coastline") of any country. Its [border with the United States](/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_States_border "Canada–United States border") is the longest international land border. The country is characterized by a wide range of both [meteorologic](/wiki/Temperature_in_Canada "Temperature in Canada") and [geological](/wiki/Geography_of_Canada "Geography of Canada") regions. With [a population](/wiki/Population_of_Canada "Population of Canada") of over 41 million, it has widely varying population densities, with the majority residing in [its urban areas](/wiki/List_of_the_largest_population_centres_in_Canada "List of the largest population centres in Canada") and large areas being sparsely populated. Its capital is [Ottawa](/wiki/Ottawa "Ottawa") and [its three largest metropolitan areas](/wiki/List_of_census_metropolitan_areas_and_agglomerations_in_Canada "List of census metropolitan areas and agglomerations in Canada") are [Toronto](/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), [Montreal](/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"), and [Vancouver](/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver").
